fact: A data-policy training session held on 24 September 2025 in Antananarivo, part of a multi-day workshop run by Team Europe's Data Governance in Africa Action, brought together over 50 delegates from SADC, SATA, SAPOA and CRASA to discuss joint approaches to regional cooperation, data-sharing agreements and harmonised cross-border regulation.

In the week of 27 July 2020 the African Union's first online school on Internet governance, run with PRIDA to support countries such as Madagascar, was given to the 17-member organising committee of Madagascar's national Internet Governance Forum; the AU Commission/PRIDA also spoke at the forum's opening and closing on 27-28 August 2020.

Madagascar sent a delegation led by the Minister of Labour, Employment and the Public Service to the SADC annual public service general assembly in Eswatini, 28-31 August 2026, where member states discussed digital transformation and digitalisation of public services among other topics; attendance only, no agreement signed.
Smart Africa names Madagascar among the 19 signatories of the SATA Declaration on digital trust and cross-border interoperability.
